title: Monitoring the immune response to vaccination with an inactivated vaccine associated to bovine neonatal pancytopenia by deep sequencing transcriptome analysis in cattle.
ehr_evidence: The data source was whole blood samples collected from cattle and analyzed by next-generation RNA sequencing (RNAseq); no electronic/computerised individual-level health records were used.
summary: An experimental longitudinal transcriptomics study of 12 cows aged 3-5 years vaccinated with an inactivated BVDV vaccine (PregSure®), using RNAseq to characterize the whole-blood immune/transcriptome response.
key_findings: Vaccination yielded 2901 differentially expressed loci at a significance threshold of q < 0.05 (1879 upregulated, 1022 downregulated).
A novel previously unannotated locus XLOC_032517 showed a highly significant 3.51-fold upregulation after vaccination (p < 0.0001).
Three cows never vaccinated with PregSure® showed significantly lower XLOC_032517 expression than the 12 vaccinated cows (p = 0.008).
Pathway analysis revealed a coordinated immune response to viral dsRNA (RIG-I-like receptor, TLR3, EIF2/PKR pathways) and upregulation of T cell receptor signaling.
No coordinated transcriptomic pattern indicating activation of the alloantigen response pathway was identified.
captured_features: KEGG and Ingenuity canonical pathway enrichment
Predicted upstream regulators (z-score, p-value of overlap)
XLOC_032517 expression across blood and tissues
pathologies_diseases: Bovine neonatal pancytopenia (BNP) (context; four cows had calves with clinical BNP)
study_design: Experimental longitudinal (before vs. 14 days after vaccination) transcriptomics study
population: 12 lactating and non-lactating cows aged 3-5 years, German Holstein × Charolais crossbred, kept on the FBN Dummerstorf experimental dairy farm
limitations: Small sample size (n = 12) limiting statistical power.
Whole-blood transcriptome does not capture peripheral/tissue-restricted immune regulation.
No coordinated alloantigen response identified, leaving BNP pathogenesis unresolved.
